speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I understand you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues. To begin our assessment, can you describe exactly how this swelling started and if you have experienced any pain, redness, or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the onset in an 18-month-old without trauma and the family history are concerning. Have you noticed the swelling fluctuate in size or change color, and does the knee feel warm to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Swelling of the right knee. I also have No recent trauma or injury, Familial history of similar symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Leukemia (specifically Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia presenting with a pathologic fracture or bone marrow expansion) or a rare genetic bone disorder like OI or HSD, but given the age and family history, we must rule out malignancy first. However, the specific presentation of an 18-month-old with knee swelling, no trauma, and a family history of similar issues strongly suggests a genetic bone condition. Let me clarify the family history: did the uncle suffer from fractures or deformities? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential. REQUEST IMAGES: X-ray of the right knee.
